The capture is real output from npm 11.18.0 and node v26.6.0 against this repository at v0.1.0, plus the failing direction: npm pack in a directory with no package.json exits 254 and prints no JSON array, which is the arm the parser's ok/reason branch exists for. It also records a fact the SOURCE would mislead a reader about: on this npm the `--json` paths carry NO `package/` prefix, so the strip in packListing is a no-op kept for older npm. The named tests read the capture and assert that shape rather than a hand-written one (CLAUDE.md warning 10). MEMBERS REWRITTEN IN FIX ROUND 1 because the inventory itself was rewritten: member 0 now derives the name from the FIRST node_modules segment instead of the last, so a nested copy is inventoried under its parent's name and the set no longer matches what M3-P1 recorded; member 1 reads every licence as a constant, so the set is complete and the classification is wrong. Two wrong-answer states at two different points. RESIDUE: the capture fixes the successful shape and one failure, and does not enumerate npm's other failure modes; a pack that exited 0 and printed malformed JSON is handled by the parser's catch and is not represented here.
